# How dimensions work in the Monecraft engine today

**The load-bearing fact:** the engine is **single-dimension by construction**. One `GameEngine` owns exactly one `VoxelWorld` for one `DimensionId`, fixed for the engine's life. "Travelling" is not an in-engine state swap — it serializes, remounts the React tree, and **boots a brand-new engine** in the target dimension. This is why the nether is single-player-only, and it's the central obstacle to multiplayer nether.

## 1. State shape

- `GameState` holds **one** `world: VoxelWorld` and one `dimension: DimensionId` — `lib/game/engine/state.ts:306` and `:313`. The doc comment there is explicit: *"one live dimension per engine — `world` and every voxel-indexed collection are in ITS space… Fixed for the engine's life; portal travel boots a fresh engine."* There is **no** second `VoxelWorld`, no `worlds: Map<DimensionId, VoxelWorld>` anywhere.
- `DimensionId = "overworld" | "nether"` — `lib/game/types.ts:365`.
- **World creation** happens once in the constructor, eagerly for whichever dimension the engine is booting: `const world = new VoxelWorld(size.x, size.y, size.z, seed)` then `if (dimension === "nether") generateNetherWorld(world); else generateWorld(world, this.worldType)` — `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts:322-324`. So the nether volume is created **eagerly at engine boot, but only when this engine's dimension is nether** — i.e. lazily from the world's perspective (the nether engine only comes into existence on first travel). The overworld world is never resident while the nether engine runs, and vice-versa.
- **Volume/byte sizes:** both dimensions use the same constants — `WORLD_SIZE_X = 512`, `WORLD_SIZE_Y = 150`, `WORLD_SIZE_Z = 512` (`lib/world/blocks.ts:1-3`), consumed at `GameEngine.ts:321`. That's 512×150×512 = 39,321,600 voxels → `blocks: Uint8Array` ≈ 39.3 MB **plus** `light: Uint8Array` ≈ 39.3 MB (`lib/world/voxelWorld.ts:34-35`). Overworld and nether are **identical in size**; the nether is not a smaller volume. Coordinates map **1:1** (no ×8 Minecraft scale — see portal travel below). There is no separate nether size constant in `lib/game/config.ts`.

## 2. Dimension keying

Because only one dimension is ever live in an engine, "dimension-keyed" splits into two buckets:

**Persisted per-dimension** (each lives in a `DimensionSection`, `lib/game/types.ts:430-436`): block-change journal (`changes`), containers/chests (`blockEntities`), looted-worldgen-chest set (`lootedChests`), mobs (`mobs`), vehicles (`vehicles`). The overworld's section **is the top level** of the save; the nether's lives under `dimensions.nether`.

**Live on `GameState`** (so implicitly scoped to the one live dimension, and mostly session-only / re-derived, not dimension-persisted):
- `containers: Map<number, InventorySlot[]>` — `state.ts:361`
- `primedTnt: Map<number, number>` (session-only) — `state.ts:363`
- `mobs: MobState[]`, `nextMobId` — `state.ts:386-387`
- `projectiles` (arrows/fireballs, session-only) — `state.ts:390-391`
- `thrownSpears` — `state.ts:388`
- `vehicles`, `mountedVehicleId` — `state.ts:395-397`
- `redstone: RedstoneState` (session-only, re-derived from the grid) — `state.ts:422-434`
- Dungeon/shipwreck/treasure/buried-treasure/village site sets — `state.ts:366-379` — all **re-derived from the seed each load**, and **skipped entirely for the nether** (`GameEngine.ts:328-334`: nether gets empty dungeon/shipwreck/treasure/village sets).
- Lighting: `world.light` is a **derived cache, never serialized**, rebaked per boot (`GameEngine.ts:354`, `voxelWorld.ts:21-27`).

**Global (shared world time / not dimension-split):** `dayClock` is top-level in the save and shared across dimensions (`GameEngine.ts:472` comment, `dayNight.ts:18`). Per-player fields (inventory, hearts, xp, advancements, `spawnPoint`, and crucially `dimension` + one-shot `portalArrival`) live on `SavedPlayer` — `types.ts:376-393`.

Note `MobState` and `ProjectileState` carry **no dimension field** (`state.ts:111-157`, `:164-185`) — they don't need one because the whole mob list belongs to the one live dimension. `ProjectileState.kind: "fireball"` even carries a comment (`state.ts:180-184`) that nether mobs "never exist in an online world, so it never crosses the wire."

## 3. Portal travel

All portal logic is in `lib/game/engine/systems/portal.ts`. The full sequence:

- **Ignite** — `tryIgnitePortal` (`portal.ts:106-132`): right-click flint & steel on obsidian → raycast the struck face → `findPortalFrame` validates a full obsidian border around a 2×3…4×4 interior (`portal.ts:34-85`; limits `PORTAL_MIN/MAX_INTERIOR` in `config.ts:247-248`). On success `fillPortalFrame` writes `NetherPortal` cells through `blockChanges` and emits `{type:"portalLit"}`. **The gate:** an `allowed` boolean param — when false it emits `{type:"portalDenied", reason:"online"}` instead (`portal.ts:124-127`).
- **Step-in / dwell** — `tickPortalDwell` (`portal.ts:179-204`): standing in a `NetherPortal` cell accumulates `player.timers.portalDwellSeconds`; at `PORTAL_DWELL_SECONDS` (3s, `config.ts:250`) it latches (`portalLatched`, so no ping-pong) and emits **`{type:"dimensionTravel", target: state.dimension === "nether" ? "overworld" : "nether", anchor: frame.base}`** (`portal.ts:203`). Travel-time re-validates the frame; a broken frame is cleared instead (`portal.ts:198-202`).
- **State swap / renderer swap** happens in the **React shell, not the engine** — `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts:481-493`: on a `dimensionTravel` event it arms `skipUnmountSaveRef`, calls `gameEngine.serializeForTravel(target, anchor)`, writes that save, and after 60 ms calls `onReloadWorld()` to **remount**. The remount reboots a fresh `GameEngine` (`useMinecraftGame.ts:275-285`) and a fresh `GameRenderer` built for the new dimension's profile (`useMinecraftGame.ts:360`).
- **Position mapping / pairing** — coordinates are **1:1** (`portal.ts:212` "1:1 coordinates"). On the next boot, `serializeForTravel` (`GameEngine.ts:1333-1341`) has stamped the local player with `dimension: target`, `position: anchor`, and a one-shot `portalArrival: anchor`. The constructor consumes it via `restorePortalArrival` → `ensureArrivalPortal` (`GameEngine.ts:349-350`), which **searches** for an existing portal within `PORTAL_SEARCH_RADIUS` (24, `config.ts:252`) near the mapped anchor, and **builds** a stone-pad + lit 2×3 frame if none found (`portal.ts:213-265`). Arrival latches the player's dwell so they don't immediately travel back (`GameEngine.ts:483-486`).
- **Events emitted:** `portalLit`, `portalDenied` (reason `"online"` | `"invalidFrame"`), `dimensionTravel` — declared in `state.ts:616-618`.

## 4. The online refusal — exact location

The gate is a single getter:

```
private get portalsEnabled(): boolean {
  return this.authority === "local" && !this.replica;
}
```
— **`lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts:535-537`**. Comment: *"Portals work in local single-player only (for now): the server engine and every replica refuse ignition, so an online world can never strand a player in a dimension the room doesn't simulate."*

It gates **both** ends:
- **Ignition:** passed as the `allowed` arg — `GameEngine.ts:1035`: `if (tryIgnitePortal(state, player, this.emit, this.portalsEnabled, this.rng)) break;` → emits `portalDenied/"online"` when false.
- **Travel/dwell:** `GameEngine.ts:801`: `if (this.portalsEnabled) tickPortalDwell(...)` — an online engine never even accumulates dwell.

So the block is engine-side and fires for **both** the server engine (`authority: "server"`) and every client replica (`replica: true`). The shell surfaces it at `useMinecraftGame.ts:510-511` ("Portals aren't available in online worlds yet"). The root cause is structural: the server room constructs **one** engine with no dimension option → defaults to overworld (`server/room.ts:172-181`), and has no mechanism to simulate a second world.

## 5. Save format (v18)

- `SaveData` (v18) — `types.ts:447-451`: top-level world fields **are the overworld's**; other dimensions live under optional `dimensions?: { nether?: DimensionSection }`; plus optional top-level `worldgenVersion`.
- `serialize()` — `GameEngine.ts:1279-1325`: builds the **live** dimension's `DimensionSection`, then branches: a **nether** engine writes the held-foreign overworld half at the top level verbatim and puts live nether state under `dimensions.nether` (`:1301-1314`); an **overworld** engine writes live state at the top level and re-emits any held `foreignDimensions` verbatim (`:1316-1323`). The verbatim pass-through is via `foreignDimensions` / `foreignOverworld`, captured at boot (`GameEngine.ts:260-261`, `:307-320`) — this is how the **server room round-trips a world's nether builds without ever simulating them**.
- **A world that never visited the nether:** `dimensions` is simply **absent** — `save.ts:282` ("`dimensions` absent means the world has never had a nether visit"), and `dimensionSectionOf` returns `{ changes: [] }` for a missing section (`save.ts:322-327`). Players have no `dimension` field → `restorePlayerDimension` defaults `"overworld"` (`save.ts:333-334`). So a pre-nether world is byte-compatible.
- **Migration** `migrateSaveV17toV18` is a **pure version bump** — `save.ts:288-289`, no data moves.
- `worldgenVersion` (currently 11) governs staleness for **both** dimensions together: a mismatch discards every dimension's world half and reboots from seed (`applyWorldgenGuard`, run first in the constructor `GameEngine.ts:288`); an absent stamp is grandfathered (`save.ts:293-312`, `docs/save-format.md:35-36`).
- ⚠️ **Drift trap** documented at `types.ts:427-428` and `docs/save-format.md:36`: any field added to `serialize()`'s world half must also be added to `DimensionSection` or it silently stays overworld-global.

## 6. Respawn / death in the nether

Respawn placement is **dimension-relative and stays in-dimension** — `GameEngine.ts:1754-1772`:
- If the player has a `spawnPoint` (bed) **and that cell in the current world is a `Bed`**, respawn there (`:1756-1759`). In the nether the overworld bed's voxel index won't be a `Bed` block in the nether world, so this **falls through** (there is no bed-explosion behavior — it just isn't honored).
- Else respawn at `randomLandPointNear(state.world, this.surfaceYAt, sizeX/2, sizeZ/2, …)` (`:1761-1762`) — and `this.surfaceYAt` is `createNetherFloorYAt` for a nether engine (`GameEngine.ts:342`, `spawn.ts:28`). **So dying in the nether respawns you at a random point near the center of the nether** — you are not kicked back to the overworld. This is the "open design point" your memory flagged: there is currently no cross-dimension respawn and no bed-in-nether handling. Respawn never changes `state.dimension`.

Death freeze is authority-dependent: local SP freezes the world during the respawn countdown (`GameEngine.ts:664-665`); a server never freezes for one death and runs each player's countdown in their per-player step (`:730-733`).

## 7. Renderer

The renderer does **not** live-switch dimensions — it is **rebuilt per dimension** because swap-on-travel remounts it. `lib/game/render/dimensionProfiles.ts` defines a per-dimension `DimensionProfile` (sky colors, `fogNear/fogFar`, `skyLightFloor`, `celestials`, `precipitation`) — `dimensionProfiles.ts:9-50`; the doc comment (`:3-8`) states these are **construction-time constants — no uniforms, no live switching** (the shader **bakes `skyLightFloor` into its source string**).

In `GameRenderer.ts`: the profile is a `readonly` field set in the constructor (`:77`, `:123-131`); `patchVoxelLighting` bakes `skyLightFloor` into the material shader (`:49-58`, `:166-167`); the `SkyView` and precipitation layers are created **only if** `profile.celestials` / `profile.precipitation` (`:185-186`) — the nether has neither. Fog color/`far` derive from the profile each frame (`:658-659`). `GameRenderer.create(node, DIMENSION_PROFILES[gameEngine.state.dimension])` is called at `useMinecraftGame.ts:360`. Terrain is a full mesh rebuild driven by `state.worldMeshDirty` → `rebuildWorldMesh` (`GameRenderer.ts:625-628`); on a dimension change the whole renderer (and its single mesh) is disposed and recreated, so there is **no** separate-scenes or dual-mesh mechanism. Minimap colors also branch on dimension (`lib/game/render/minimapColors.ts`).

## 8. Engine step / tick

**The engine ticks only ONE dimension per step — the one it holds.** There is no loop over dimensions; `step()` (`GameEngine.ts:617`) advances the single `state.world` and its single mob/vehicle/projectile/redstone collections. A second dimension has **no ticking representation at all** while it isn't the live one — the other dimension exists only as inert serialized bytes (`foreignDimensions`/`foreignOverworld`). **This is the critical gap for multiplayer**: a server that must simulate players split across dimensions has nowhere to run the second world today — one `GameEngine` = one world, and the server builds exactly one (`server/room.ts:172-181`, overworld).

Per-dimension **behavior** that already exists (all keyed off `state.dimension` within the single live engine):
- **Day/night:** `dimensionDaylightAt` pins nether daylight to `NETHER_DAYLIGHT = 0.22` (`dayNight.ts:20-22`, `config.ts:243`), below the hostile-spawn threshold, so hostiles are perpetual without special-casing. The `dayClock` itself keeps ticking (shared world time).
- **Spawn director:** `spawnDirector.ts:118-129` swaps to a hostile-only nether roster (`imp`, `scorcher`), skips aquatic spawns (`:189`), and the ambient roster swaps at `:291`. Nether mob templates in `lib/game/mobs.ts:188-220` (`imp`, `scorcher` with fireball).
- **Weather** kept clear in the nether; **sleep** denied in the nether (`sleepDenied` reason `"dimension"`, `state.ts:605`).
- Random ticks, redstone, breeding, raids all run on the one live world (`GameEngine.ts:702-718`); a **replica** simulates none of it — it only predicts local movement/mining and smooths the day clock (`GameEngine.ts:636-657`).

---

### Bottom line for "Nether in multiplayer"
The single hard blocker is architectural, not a one-line flag: `portalsEnabled` (`GameEngine.ts:535`) refuses portals precisely because **one engine simulates one dimension** (`state.ts:306-313`) and travel is implemented as a **full engine+renderer remount** driven by the SP React shell (`useMinecraftGame.ts:481-493`) via `serializeForTravel` (`GameEngine.ts:1333`). The server room runs a single overworld engine (`server/room.ts:172`). Supporting multiplayer nether means either (a) running multiple `GameEngine` instances server-side (one per dimension) with a cross-engine travel handoff and per-dimension client replicas/renderers, or (b) generalizing `GameState` to hold multiple worlds and ticking each. The save format is already dimension-ready (`DimensionSection`, `dimensions.nether`, per-player `dimension`), and per-dimension gameplay (daylight, spawns, mobs, renderer profiles) is already parameterized by `state.dimension` — the missing piece is **concurrent multi-dimension simulation and a travel path that doesn't remount the whole client**.</result>

# Nether in Multiplayer — Plan (DRAFT — exploration in progress)

## Context

v0.16.0 is live and the board is clean (no open PRs, upstream sync #15 merged). The user asked "what's next?" and picked the recommended direction: **unlock the Nether in multiplayer**. The v0.16 flagship feature — a full second dimension with portals, netherrack/glowstone worldgen, the blazite post-diamond tier, and imp/scorcher mobs — is single-player only today: the server engine and every online replica refuse portal ignition. The co-op audience (the other major investment: v0.13 multiplayer, MP v2 parity, protocol v3 melee lag comp, Fly.io deploy) cannot see it at all.

Goal: two players in an online world can ignite and use portals, split across dimensions (one in the overworld, one in the Nether), and everything replicates correctly — likely as protocol v4 with a synchronized deploy (precedent: the v3 lag-comp deploy).

Known design questions to resolve in this plan:
- Server room memory: ~74 MB/room today, 512 MB VM, MAX_ROOMS 3 — a second world volume per room pressures the ceiling (lazy nether generation? smaller nether volume? cap adjustment?).
- Dimension-keyed replication: which tick contents (block changes, mob poses, player poses, vehicles, projectiles) must be filtered/keyed by dimension.
- Cross-dimension concerns: chat (global), sleep-skips-night (overworld-only players?), melee lag comp across dimension boundaries, in-Nether respawn (open design point from the single-player epic).
- Save: online worlds persist via cloud saves — the v18 nether sections must round-trip.

## Exploration findings — client net replica (done)

- Client online = a **full local GameEngine in replica mode** (`authority: "local", replica: true`, built from WELCOME seed) — `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts:279-296`. Replica `step()` simulates only local-player prediction + cosmetic mining; mobs/TNT/projectiles/vitals are replicated (`GameEngine.ts:636-646`).
- **No dimension on the wire anywhere**: `WelcomeMessage`/`WorldSync`/`TickMessage`/`RosterEntry` (`protocol.ts:84`)/`PlayerPose` (`protocol.ts:137`) all lack it. WorldSync is one flat gzipped block diff over one volume (`protocol.ts:107-121`, applied `NetworkSession.ts:355-380`).
- **Dimension is construction-time** on engine (`state.dimension`, `state.ts:309-313`) and renderer (`DIMENSION_PROFILES`, `lib/game/render/dimensionProfiles.ts:28-50`; `skyLightFloor` baked into shader source → renderer rebuild required). SP travel does a full engine+renderer **remount** via `serializeForTravel` (`GameEngine.ts:1333-1341`) + `onReloadWorld`; online has no analog. Minimap reads `state.dimension` live each sync (`minimap.ts:55`); music keys off daylight+biome, NOT dimension (`audioDirector.ts:449`) — gap.
- Remote players: `remotePlayerVisuals.sync` renders ALL of `state.players` unconditionally at raw coords (`remotePlayerVisuals.ts:69-119`) — no per-player dimension exists. Server pose validation assumes one volume (`applyRemotePose`, `GameEngine.ts:555-579`).
- Refusals: `portalsEnabled = authority === "local" && !replica` (`GameEngine.ts:530-537`); ignite denied with `portalDenied reason:"online"` (`portal.ts:124-126`) → toast (`useMinecraftGame.ts:510-512`); `dimensionTravel` event handler gated `!online` (`useMinecraftGame.ts:481-493`). SP save carries other-dimension data as inert `foreignDimensions` (`GameEngine.ts:253-261, 301-334`).
- Event/toast seam for "X entered the Nether": tick `ev` stream → `drainEvents` → `useMinecraftGame.ts:457-544` switch (like advancement toasts). Chat/roster/status subscription patterns at `NetworkSession.ts:614-635, 753-755`.
- Tests: two-context e2e pattern in `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` (own helpers `:24-72`, real Next+Bun-server stack via `playwright.config.ts:27-47`); SP `e2e/portal.e2e.ts` asserts dimension flip via remount (not reusable online). Net unit tests: `lib/net/*.test.ts`, `server/room.test.ts`, `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts`; soak: `scripts/loadSim.ts`.

## 1. Architecture decision

**Recommendation: two engines per room ("dimension shards"). Confirmed, with one prerequisite that makes it cheap: skip the light bake on headless engines.**

Alternatives considered:

| Option | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Two engines per room** (chosen) | ✅ | Preserves the load-bearing invariant documented at `lib/game/engine/state.ts:308-313` ("one live dimension per engine — `world` and every voxel-indexed collection are in ITS space"). Every engine system (spawn directors, mob AI, redstone, random ticks, portal dwell, `surfaceYAt`, save serialization) already works per-dimension unmodified. The Room becomes a router; the engines don't change shape. |
| B. Multi-world `GameState` (one engine, two worlds) | ❌ | `state.world`, `state.mobs`, `state.blockChanges`, `state.dimension`, `state.containers` etc. are singletons read by ~20 system files. Every system signature would need a dimension context; `serialize()`, `blockChanges`, `surfaceYAt`, and the spawn directors would all be rewritten. Enormous diff, maximum regression risk, and it breaks SP too. |
| C. Reconnect-per-travel (nether = a second room; client disconnects and rejoins) | ❌ | Two rooms per world doubles pressure on `MAX_ROOMS`; **two rooms would write one `worlds` row** (persist races in `server/persistence.ts`); chat/roster/kick/owner-settings span dimensions so cross-room plumbing is needed anyway; tickets are per-world (`lib/online/worldsService.ts:368`) so the registry would need a dimension key; and the UX is a full disconnect (reconnect ladder, "Reconnecting…" modal) per portal. The in-band path instead reuses the join machinery (`welcome`-less: `dim` + a fresh gzipped `WorldSync`) on a live socket. |

**Key enabling fact (verified):** the only reader of `world.light` in the entire codebase is the renderer — `lib/world/meshing.ts:183` via `VoxelWorld.getSky/getBlockLight` (`lib/world/voxelWorld.ts:64-73`). No gameplay system reads voxel light (hostile spawn/burn gates read `state.daylight` from `dayNight.ts`, not the light array). `blockChanges.set` *writes* light via `applyEdit` (`lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts:47`) but nothing server-side reads it back. So a headless engine can skip `computeFullLight` (`GameEngine.ts:354`) **and** drop the 39.3 MB `light` array (replace with a zero-length `Uint8Array`, guard the `applyEdit` call). That halves per-engine memory (~78 MB → ~40 MB) and removes the full-world BFS bake from server engine construction — **a two-engine room then costs roughly what a one-engine room costs today (~80 MB)**, so no Fly resizing is required (`server/fly.toml`: MAX_ROOMS=3 @ 512 MB stands).

**Client side:** the swap is in-band. On travel the server sends a new `dim` message + a fresh `WorldSync` for the target dimension; `NetworkSession` builds a **new replica engine** (its ctor already accepts `dimension` for save-less boots, `GameEngine.ts:304`), rebinds its internal `state`/`self` closures, and fires an `onDimension` callback; `GameShell` bumps a nonce in the `MinecraftGame` key so the renderer (whose `DIMENSION_PROFILES` choice is construction-time, `useMinecraftGame.ts:360`) rebuilds. This requires moving `session.dispose()` ownership from `useMinecraftGame`'s effect cleanup (`useMinecraftGame.ts:570`) to `GameShell` (which created the session) — otherwise the swap-remount would kill the socket.

- **Client→server:** `pose` += `d: DimensionId` (required); `cmd` += `d: DimensionId` (required). Server drops mismatched frames silently (travel race guard — no `forcePose` for these).
- **Server→client:** `welcome` += `dimension`; `worldSync` += `dimension`; `RosterEntry` += `dim` (rides welcome/worldSync/playerJoined); new `dim { dimension, tick, dayClock }` (traveler-only, followed by the target `WorldSync` binary frame); new `playerDim { id, dimension }` (broadcast).

## 4. Edge cases (proposed behaviors)

1. **Join while saved-in-nether** — `join()` ensures the nether shard (sync ctor inside the async join), seats the player there, `welcome.dimension:"nether"`, nether `WorldSync`; client boots a nether replica; renderer profile follows automatically (`useMinecraftGame.ts:360`).
2. **Travel while mounted** — impossible: dwell is gated while `mountedVehicleId !== null` (Commit 2). The vehicle stays put.
3. **Pets** — do **not** travel (SP parity: mobs are per-dimension state; `serializeForTravel` leaves them behind too). The pet persists in the source dimension and resumes following on return. Documented; future enhancement.
4. **Death in nether online** — per-engine respawn stays (nether-safe via `findNetherSpawn`-backed `surfaceYAt`); bed respawn now dimension-guarded (Commit 2). Cross-dimension respawn is an explicit non-goal here (open question #1).
5. **Kick/leave while in nether** — routed by `conn.dimension`; the offline slice self-stamps `dimension:"nether"` and the player rejoins there.
6. **Portal broken while someone's in the nether** — no stranding: return-travel re-validates the frame (`tickPortalDwell` backstop, `portal.ts:198-201`) and `ensureArrivalPortal` finds-or-builds on the overworld side.
7. **Both players dwell simultaneously** — the travel queue processes both in one tick; the second finds the shard already created; each gets its own `dim`+sync. Unit-tested.
8. **Backpressure during the worldSync burst** — travel syncs bypass shedding exactly like join syncs; a conn past the 1 MB kick threshold is already on the strike path. The traveler simply misses that tick's source-shard frame (they've left it).
9. **Prediction ledger across the swap** — new engine + `ledger.clear()` + `delayCtl.reset()` + buffer wipes in `adoptDimension`; stale poses/cmds are dropped server-side via `d`.
10. **Chat & roster** — global; roster entries carry `dim`; the panel shows "· Nether".
11. **Owner-kick of a nether player** — `kick`→`leave` routed by shard; unit-tested.
12. **Peaceful switch** — room mirrors `setWorldDifficulty` into every shard so hostiles despawn in **both** engines; unit-tested.
13. **Travel toast for others** — `playerDim` → synthetic `playerDimension` event → `flashMessage` in the drain (`useMinecraftGame.ts` switch).
14. **Reconnect mid/post-travel** — resumed `welcome.dimension` compared against the replica; mismatch triggers `adoptDimension` before the resync.
15. **Cross-dimension mobsKeyframe** — structurally impossible after shard scoping (would otherwise mass-prune the wrong replica's mobs).
16. **Sleep** — only overworld players gate the skip (free from the split); `wakeToMorning`'s clock jump mirrors to the nether shard each tick.

- **Light bake resolved:** renderer-only (see §1). Headless skip saves ~39.3 MB + the full-world BFS per server engine.
- **Budget:** engine ≈ 39.3 MB blocks (+ objects); two-shard room ≈ 80 MB ≈ today's documented single-engine budget (~74 MB). **Keep `server/fly.toml` at MAX_ROOMS=3 / 512 MB** (worst case ~240 MB + Bun runtime); update the fly.toml comment and `docs/online.md` capacity note ("~80 MB per nether-active room after the light-skip; 6 rooms ≈ 1 GB" replaces the current text at `docs/online.md:249-253`).
- **Lifecycle:** lazy create on first travel/nether-join; linger-evict (60 s default) after the last nether player leaves — persist the section, drop the engine. One-time synchronous ctor hitch on the shared tick thread (all rooms pause briefly); measure with loadSim and document; the same class of hitch already exists at room load (`roomRegistry.ts:38-45`).

- **Unit — engine:** headless light-skip; ctor dimension override; `ensureArrival`; `setWorldDifficulty`; mounted-dwell gate; dimension-guarded bed respawn.
- **Unit — protocol:** v4 field round-trips; `d` validation on pose/cmd; new message shapes.

- **Unit — session (`NetworkSession.test.ts`, FakeSocket):** the swap (engine replaced, socket alive, ledger/buffers cleared, self position adopted, `d` stamping flips); `playerDim` prune/adopt; nether welcome; stale-sync ignore; reconnect-into-other-dimension.
- **e2e:** new two-context nether journey (Phase 6); existing `multiplayer.e2e.ts` and SP `portal.e2e.ts` stay green.
- **Soak:** `loadSim` before/after with a nether-active room; report `slowestTickMs` p95 + `kbOutPerSec` in the PR.

Covered per-phase and in Commit 10: `protocol.md` (v4 + bump/rollout), `deploy.md` (protocol-bump runbook — new), `online.md` (nether co-op + capacity), `architecture.md` (shards + client swap + dispose ownership), `manual.md` (portals now online), `tuning.md` (linger config, mounted gate), `testing.md` (coverage map), `save-format.md` (v18 **unchanged**; optional `spawnPoint.dimension` addition; server now writes `dimensions.nether`), `CHANGELOG.md`.

# Implementation Plan: Nether in Multiplayer (`feat/nether-online`, protocol v3→v4)

## 1. Architecture decision

**Recommendation: two engines per room ("dimension shards"). Confirmed, with one prerequisite that makes it cheap: skip the light bake on headless engines.**

Alternatives considered:

| Option | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Two engines per room** (chosen) | ✅ | Preserves the load-bearing invariant documented at `lib/game/engine/state.ts:308-313` ("one live dimension per engine — `world` and every voxel-indexed collection are in ITS space"). Every engine system (spawn directors, mob AI, redstone, random ticks, portal dwell, `surfaceYAt`, save serialization) already works per-dimension unmodified. The Room becomes a router; the engines don't change shape. |
| B. Multi-world `GameState` (one engine, two worlds) | ❌ | `state.world`, `state.mobs`, `state.blockChanges`, `state.dimension`, `state.containers` etc. are singletons read by ~20 system files. Every system signature would need a dimension context; `serialize()`, `blockChanges`, `surfaceYAt`, and the spawn directors would all be rewritten. Enormous diff, maximum regression risk, and it breaks SP too. |
| C. Reconnect-per-travel (nether = a second room; client disconnects and rejoins) | ❌ | Two rooms per world doubles pressure on `MAX_ROOMS`; **two rooms would write one `worlds` row** (persist races in `server/persistence.ts`); chat/roster/kick/owner-settings span dimensions so cross-room plumbing is needed anyway; tickets are per-world (`lib/online/worldsService.ts:368`) so the registry would need a dimension key; and the UX is a full disconnect (reconnect ladder, "Reconnecting…" modal) per portal. The in-band path instead reuses the join machinery (`welcome`-less: `dim` + a fresh gzipped `WorldSync`) on a live socket. |

**Key enabling fact (verified):** the only reader of `world.light` in the entire codebase is the renderer — `lib/world/meshing.ts:183` via `VoxelWorld.getSky/getBlockLight` (`lib/world/voxelWorld.ts:64-73`). No gameplay system reads voxel light (hostile spawn/burn gates read `state.daylight` from `dayNight.ts`, not the light array). `blockChanges.set` *writes* light via `applyEdit` (`lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts:47`) but nothing server-side reads it back. So a headless engine can skip `computeFullLight` (`GameEngine.ts:354`) **and** drop the 39.3 MB `light` array (replace with a zero-length `Uint8Array`, guard the `applyEdit` call). That halves per-engine memory (~78 MB → ~40 MB) and removes the full-world BFS bake from server engine construction — **a two-engine room then costs roughly what a one-engine room costs today (~80 MB)**, so no Fly resizing is required (`server/fly.toml`: MAX_ROOMS=3 @ 512 MB stands).

**Client side:** the swap is in-band. On travel the server sends a new `dim` message + a fresh `WorldSync` for the target dimension; `NetworkSession` builds a **new replica engine** (its ctor already accepts `dimension` for save-less boots, `GameEngine.ts:304`), rebinds its internal `state`/`self` closures, and fires an `onDimension` callback; `GameShell` bumps a nonce in the `MinecraftGame` key so the renderer (whose `DIMENSION_PROFILES` choice is construction-time, `useMinecraftGame.ts:360`) rebuilds. The WebSocket never drops. This requires moving `session.dispose()` ownership from `useMinecraftGame`'s effect cleanup (`useMinecraftGame.ts:570`) to `GameShell` (which created the session) — otherwise the swap-remount would kill the socket.

---

## 2. Phased commit plan (bisectable; lint/typecheck/test green per commit)

### Phase 1 — engine prep (3 small commits, no online behavior change)

**Commit 1: `feat(engine): skip the light bake and light array on headless engines`**
- `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts:352-354` — gate `world.light = computeFullLight(world)` on `!this.headless`; for headless set `world.light = new Uint8Array(0)`.
- `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts:47` — guard: `if (world.light.length !== 0) applyEdit(world, world.light, x, y, z);`.
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md` (lighting note), `docs/online.md` memory numbers, `docs/tuning.md` if it mentions the ~74 MB figure.
- Tests: headless engine has empty light + `blockChanges.set` still journals/relights nothing; a local engine still bakes (existing `lighting.test.ts` untouched).

**Commit 2: `fix(engine): gate portal dwell while mounted; dimension-stamp the bed spawn point`**
- `lib/game/engine/systems/portal.ts` (`tickPortalDwell`, ~line 179) — early-return when `player.mountedVehicleId !== null` (a boat parked in a portal must not fire travel; server `removePlayer` un-riders on handoff but never traveling mounted is simpler and fixes SP too).

"overworld"` matches `state.dimension`).
- Docs: `docs/save-format.md` (optional field), CHANGELOG.
- Tests: dwell no-op while mounted; nether death ignores an overworld bed.

### Phase 2 — protocol v4

**Commit 4: `feat(net): protocol v4 — dimension on the wire`**
- `lib/net/protocol.ts`:
  - `PROTOCOL_VERSION = 4` (line 20). Tickets need no change — `worldsService.ts:368` mints `pv: PROTOCOL_VERSION` and `server/index.ts:97-99` checks both.
  - `PoseMessage` and `CmdMessage` gain required `d: DimensionId` — the travel race guard (the server drops any pose/cmd whose `d` ≠ the sender's current dimension, so in-flight frames sent before the client processed the swap can't force-pose-fight or raycast into the wrong world). Update `readClientMessage` validators (`d` must be `"overworld" | "nether"`).
  - `RosterEntry` gains `dim: DimensionId` (welcome/worldSync/playerJoined all reuse it → roster UI shows location).
  - `WelcomeMessage` gains `dimension: DimensionId` (the recipient's own).
  - `WorldSync` gains `dimension: DimensionId` (which world half this sync describes — guards a stale resync racing a swap).

    - `DimensionMessage { t:"dim"; dimension: DimensionId; tick: number; dayClock: number }` — sent to the traveler, immediately followed by the target dimension's gzipped `WorldSync`.
    - `PlayerDimensionMessage { t:"playerDim"; id: string; dimension: DimensionId }` — broadcast on any travel (roster + replica prune/adopt).
- `lib/game/engine/state.ts` — new `GameEvent` variant `{ type: "playerDimension"; playerId: PlayerId; dimension: DimensionId }` (client-synthesized from `playerDim` for the toast seam; never emitted by engines).
- Temporarily fill the new fields with `"overworld"` constants at existing call sites (`room.ts` welcome/worldSync/roster; `NetworkSession` pose/cmd) so this commit compiles and behaves identically.
- `scripts/loadSim.ts` — stamp `d:"overworld"` on its hand-built pose frames (v4 validators would drop them otherwise).
- Tests: `lib/net/protocol.test.ts` — round-trips for new fields/messages; poses/cmds without `d` or with a bogus `d` are rejected.
- Docs: `docs/protocol.md` v4 section (see §3 below).

### Phase 3 — server (highest-risk file: `server/room.ts`)

**Commit 5: `refactor(server): extract the per-dimension shard structure in Room` (behavior-identical)**
- Introduce `type DimensionShard = { dimension: DimensionId; engine: GameEngine; mobHistory: MobPoseHistory; mobShadow: Map<...>; vehicleShadow: Map<...>; lastProjectileCount: number }`.
- `Room` holds `shards: Map<DimensionId, DimensionShard>` (overworld always present); keep a `get engine()` returning the overworld engine so `room.test.ts` (`room.engine.state...`, `logDump`, welcome fields) and `registry` code stay valid.
- `ClientConn` gains `dimension: DimensionId` (always `"overworld"` in this commit).
- `tick()` restructured: per-shard step → `mobHistory.record` → `consumeEvents`/`drainEdits` → pose collectors; fan-out selects the recipient's shard; `mobsKeyframe` broadcast **per shard to that shard's clients only** (critical: a cross-dimension keyframe would prune every mob on the wrong replica, since keyframes delete-by-absence — `NetworkSession.ts:603-612`); `day` read from the overworld shard.
- `collectPlayerPoses(shard, except)` iterates the shard's engine players (players in the other dimension naturally vanish from `pp`).
- `handleMessage` routes `pose`/`cmd`/`resync` through `shardOf(conn)`; drop frames whose `d !== conn.dimension`. Lag-comp rewind (`room.ts:367-373`) reads the shard's `mobHistory`.
- Owner `setDifficulty` special-case: after dispatching to the sender's shard, mirror `engine.setWorldDifficulty` to every other shard.
- `buildWorldSync(shard)` includes `dimension`. `roster()` reads each conn's shard and stamps `dim`.
- `CommandLogEntry` gains optional `dim` (replay fidelity; `server/scripts/replay.ts` note).
- Tests: existing `room.test.ts` must pass unchanged (plus `d` stamped on test frames); add a per-shard keyframe scoping test.

**Commit 6: `feat(server): nether shard — portal travel, join-in-nether, persistence composition`**
- Flip the portal gate: `GameEngine.portalsEnabled` (`GameEngine.ts:535-537`) becomes `!this.replica` — server engines now ignite (via the networked `placeBlock` cmd, `GameEngine.ts:1035`) and tick dwell (`GameEngine.ts:801`); replicas still refuse (they route the cmd up). The `portalDenied/"online"` reason becomes vestigial (keep it defensively).
- `ensureShard("nether")`: lazily construct `new GameEngine({ save: this.composeSave(), dimension: "nether", authority: "server", headless: true, bootPlayer: false, seed/worldType/difficulty/hardcore })`. Construction is synchronous (~worldgen only, no light bake after Commit 1) — a one-time tick hitch; measure and document. Also created at `join()` when the reconnecting player's saved slice says `dimension:"nether"`.
- Travel handoff — in `tick()`, after each shard's step, filter `dimensionTravel` out of the broadcast `ev` and queue `{playerId, target, anchor}`; then `movePlayer`:
  1. `slice = sourceShard.engine.removePlayer(id)`; also filter that tick's `playerLeft`/`playerJoined` engine-event echoes for the traveler (they'd toast "left the world").
  2. `ensureShard(target)`; `const pos = targetEngine.ensureArrival(anchor)` (writes ride the target shard's journal → existing nether clients see the built portal).
  3. `targetEngine.addPlayer({id, restore: slice})`; set `position = pos + (0.5, 0, 0.5)`, `velocity = 0`, `timers.portalLatched = true`, `remoteMove = null`.
  4. `conn.dimension = target`; `conn.shadow = null` (force a full SelfDelta); `conn.lastPoseTick = tickCount`.
  5. Send to the traveler: `dim { dimension, tick, dayClock }` then `await gzipWorldSync(buildWorldSync(targetShard))` (bypasses shedding, like join).
  6. Broadcast `playerDim { id, dimension }` to everyone.
- `dayClock` mirroring: after stepping, copy the overworld engine's `dayClock` onto the nether engine (covers `wakeToMorning` jumps; both otherwise advance by identical `dt`). Sleep-skip automatically counts only overworld players (each engine's `allEligiblePlayersSleeping` sees only its own players; the nether denies sleep anyway).
- Persistence composition (`composeSave()`, used by `persist()` and nether-shard construction):
  ```
  save = overworldEngine.serialize()
  if (netherShard) { netherSave = netherShard.engine.serialize();
    save.dimensions = { ...save.dimensions, nether: netherSave.dimensions.nether };
    save.players.push(...netherSave.players); }
  else if (dormantNether) save.dimensions = { ...save.dimensions, nether: dormantNether };
  merge offlinePlayers as today (room.ts:415-417)
  ```
  Note the overworld engine's `foreignDimensions` (`GameEngine.ts:260, 307`) is captured at boot and goes stale once a nether engine runs — the room-level override above is the fix; add a comment referencing the drift trap at `types.ts:427-428`.
- Nether shard eviction: when the shard has 0 players, start a timer (`NETHER_SHARD_LINGER_MS`, propose 60 s, env-overridable like `COMMAND_LOG_SIZE`); on expiry, `dormantNether = serialize().dimensions.nether`, persist, drop the shard (and its ~40 MB).
- `leave`/`kick`: route via `conn.dimension`; the slice self-stamps `dimension` (`GameEngine.serializePlayer`, `GameEngine.ts:1250`).
- Tests (`server/room.test.ts`): travel moves the player between engines and latches; traveler receives `dim` + a nether `WorldSync` (with `dimension:"nether"` and the traveler's roster entry at the arrival); `playerDim` broadcast; a nether client's tick carries only nether `blocks`/`mp`/`ev` and never an overworld keyframe; simultaneous dwell by two players; join-while-saved-in-nether; persist composition round-trips nether builds + nether players; kick of a nether player; Peaceful despawns hostiles in both engines; lag-comp rewind partition; shard evicted after linger and rebuilt preserving builds; stale pose with `d:"overworld"` after travel is dropped (no forcePose fight).

### Phase 4 — client session (high-risk file: `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts`)

**Commit 7: `feat(net): replica dimension swap in NetworkSession`**
- Rebind-ability: `engine`, `state` (`NetworkSession.ts:289`), and `self` (`:293`) become reassignable `let` bindings — every helper (`applySelfDelta`, `applyBlocks`, `cellOf`, `upsertReplicaMob/Vehicle/Projectile`, `afterFrame`, `sendCmd`) already reads the outer variable at call time. `session.engine` becomes a getter. This closure sweep is the riskiest client change — review each capture.
- Initial build uses `welcome.dimension` (`dimension` option to the replica ctor).
- Stamp `d: currentDimension` on every outgoing pose and cmd.
- `adoptDimension(d, tick, dayClock)` (on `dim` message): build a new replica engine (same options + `dimension: d`, honoring `options.worldSize`), seat `self` (id, name, `primaryPlayerId`), reinstall `routeDispatch`, drop join echoes, clear `playerBuffers`/`mobBuffers`/`ledger`, `delayCtl.reset()`, set status `"syncing"`, fire new callback `callbacks.onDimension?.(d)`; push a synthetic toastable event for the local traveler. The following binary frame (worldSync with matching `dimension`) applies via the existing `applyWorldSync` (add: set `self.position` from the sync's own roster entry, like join does at `:352-353`; ignore a sync whose `dimension` mismatches the current engine).
- `playerDim` handler: update a `dimensions` map beside `names`; if the player's dimension ≠ ours → `engine.removePlayer(id)` + drop pose buffer; if it now matches → upsert. Push `{type:"playerDimension", playerId, dimension}` into `pendingEvents`. `applyRoster` filters by `dim` (names/dimensions kept for all, replica players only same-dimension). `RosterMember` gains `dimension`.
- Reconnect: `tryReconnectOnce` (`:673-693`) — if `resumed.dimension !== engine.state.dimension`, run `adoptDimension` before the resync applies (covers a drop mid-travel).
- Tests (`NetworkSession.test.ts`, FakeSocket): scripted `dim` + nether worldSync swaps the engine (`state.dimension === "nether"`), socket stays open, ledger/buffers cleared, self position adopted, subsequent poses carry `d:"nether"`; `playerDim` prunes a cross-dimension remote player and re-adds on return; welcome with `dimension:"nether"` boots a nether replica; a stale overworld worldSync after a swap is ignored; reconnect-into-other-dimension.

### Phase 5 — shell wiring

**Commit 8: `feat(shell): online portal travel — session ownership, dimension remount, toasts, roster tags`**
- `components/GameShell.tsx`: pass `{ onDimension: () => setDimNonce(n => n+1) }` callbacks into `connectNetworkSession` (`:281`); `play-online` key becomes `online:${world.id}:${dimNonce}` (`:411`); **move session disposal to GameShell** — `onQuitToWorlds` and `onReloadWorld` for play-online call `screen.session.dispose()` before `setScreen` (onDeleteWorld already does, `:420`).
- `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`: remove `online?.dispose()` from the effect cleanup (`:570`) — the shell owns it now (document why); add the `playerDimension` toast (“NAME entered the Nether / returned to the Overworld”) and a local travel toast on the swap; update the `portalDenied` copy (`:510-512`) — the "online" reason is no longer the normal path.
- `components/hud/RosterPanel` (and `MinecraftGame.tsx` threading): render a "· Nether" tag from `roster()[i].dimension`.
- Verify `renderer.remotePlayerInfo` re-wires on remount (it does — set per mount at `:372`).
- Tests: unit where feasible; the behavior lands in the e2e below. Run existing `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` — its assertions (players.size, roster length) remain valid (both players stay in the overworld there).

### Phase 6 — e2e + soak

**Commit 9: `test(e2e): two-context nether portal journey`**
- New `e2e/nether-online.e2e.ts` reusing `multiplayer.e2e.ts`'s helpers (extract `signUp`/`createOnlineProfile`/`waitForOnlineGame` into a shared `e2e/onlineHelpers.ts` — small refactor commit or same commit): flat + creative world (trivial geometry, instant placement).
  1. Host builds a 2×3 frame via real networked `placeBlock` cmds: a helper computes per-block stand position + yaw/pitch (all cells within `MINE_REACH` of two standing spots on flat ground; move in ≤1-block pose steps so `applyRemotePose` clamps accept), `creativeGiveItem` obsidian + `flint_and_steel`, place in bottom-bar→sides→top dependency order, polling `world.get` for the server echo after each cell. **This helper is the flakiest piece — flagged; fallback is to trim the e2e to ignition-onward (frame pre-verified by unit tests) if CI proves it unstable.**
  2. Host ignites (dispatch `placeBlock` aiming at frame obsidian) → poll both pages for `NetherPortal` (91) cells — proves server ignition + journal replication.
  3. Host walks in, dwells 3 s → poll `engine.state.dimension === "nether"`, `net.status() === "online"`, `renderedTriangles() > 0`; friend sees roster tag flip and `state.players.size === 1`.
  4. Friend follows through the same portal → both pages `players.size === 2` in the nether, both render.
  5. Host returns via the arrival portal → dimensions split again; no console errors.
  - Generous timeout (~360 s), same error-watch pattern.
- `scripts/loadSim.ts`: already `d`-stamped in Commit 4; run before/after on a nether-active room and record `slowestTickMs`/`kbOutPerSec` deltas in the PR (expect ~0 when no nether shard; +one engine step when active).

### Phase 7 — docs sweep + CHANGELOG

**Commit 10: `docs: nether online — protocol v4 narrative, ops, manual, CHANGELOG`** (page-specific edits also ride their phases per AGENTS.md; this commit is the cross-page narrative + CHANGELOG):
- `docs/protocol.md` — retitle "Wire protocol (v4)"; new fields (`d` on pose/cmd, `dim` on roster, `dimension` on welcome/worldSync), `dim`/`playerDim` messages, the travel sequence (dwell → server handoff → `dim` + worldSync → client engine swap), keyframe/tick scoping, and a **"Version bump & rollout"** section.
- `docs/deploy.md` — add the **protocol-bump runbook** (none exists today): (1) land the bump on `main` as one commit — CI deploys Vercel + Fly from the same SHA; (2) the Fly rollout SIGTERM-drains rooms (persist + `4005`); (3) reconnecting clients on the old bundle mint a v3 ticket and are refused (`4000`/`4001`, "server speaks v4") — expected; the fix is a page reload (document the user-visible message); (4) verify `/health` + a smoke join; (5) never bump `PROTOCOL_VERSION` outside a synchronized deploy.
- `docs/online.md` — nether co-op section (shards, lazy create + linger-evict, travel flow, pets/vehicles semantics); memory guidance update: ~40 MB per headless engine after the light-skip, ~80 MB worst case per nether-active room, `MAX_ROOMS=3` @ 512 MB unchanged / 6 rooms ≈ 1 GB; note the one-time construction hitch; replay-log `dim` field.
- `docs/architecture.md` — two-engines-per-room, client engine-swap lifecycle, session-disposal ownership.
- `docs/manual.md` — remove "portals are single-player only"; describe co-op travel (dwell, split parties, roster tag).
- `docs/tuning.md` — `NETHER_SHARD_LINGER_MS` (and env override), the mounted-dwell gate.
- `docs/testing.md` — coverage-map rows for the new unit suites + `nether-online.e2e.ts`.
- `docs/save-format.md` — **save format v18 unchanged** (confirmed: `dimensions.nether`, per-player `dimension`, `SavedPlayer.portalArrival` all pre-exist; the only additive change is optional `spawnPoint.dimension` from Commit 2, no version bump); note the server now actively writes `dimensions.nether`.
- `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

---

## 3. Protocol v4 delta (exact)

- `PROTOCOL_VERSION`: 3 → 4 (`lib/net/protocol.ts:20`). Ticket `pv` follows automatically (`lib/online/worldsService.ts:368`; checks at `server/index.ts:97-99`).
- **Client→server:** `pose` += `d: DimensionId` (required); `cmd` += `d: DimensionId` (required). Server drops mismatched frames silently (travel race guard — no `forcePose` for these).
- **Server→client:** `welcome` += `dimension`; `worldSync` += `dimension`; `RosterEntry` += `dim` (rides welcome/worldSync/playerJoined); new `dim { dimension, tick, dayClock }` (traveler-only, followed by the target `WorldSync` binary frame); new `playerDim { id, dimension }` (broadcast).
- **Semantics:** all tick channels (`blocks`/`ev`/`pp`/`mp`/`vp`/`prj`) and `mobsKeyframe` become dimension-scoped to the recipient; `chat`, `playerJoined`/`playerLeft`, `pong`, `day` stay global; `dimensionTravel` engine events never travel in `ev`.
- **Codec:** unchanged (JSON envelopes + the one gzipped binary frame; `gzipWorldSync` reused for the travel sync).
- **Deploy sequencing:** same-commit Vercel+Fly deploy via CI (`docs/deploy.md:187+`); add the bump runbook described in Commit 10 — the mismatch window is inherent and bounded (old bundles are refused with a clear close reason; a reload fixes).

## 4. Edge cases (proposed behaviors)

1. **Join while saved-in-nether** — `join()` ensures the nether shard (sync ctor inside the async join), seats the player there, `welcome.dimension:"nether"`, nether `WorldSync`; client boots a nether replica; renderer profile follows automatically (`useMinecraftGame.ts:360`).
2. **Travel while mounted** — impossible: dwell is gated while `mountedVehicleId !== null` (Commit 2). The vehicle stays put.
3. **Pets** — do **not** travel (SP parity: mobs are per-dimension state; `serializeForTravel` leaves them behind too). The pet persists in the source dimension and resumes following on return. Documented; future enhancement.
4. **Death in nether online** — per-engine respawn stays (nether-safe via `findNetherSpawn`-backed `surfaceYAt`); bed respawn now dimension-guarded (Commit 2). Cross-dimension respawn is an explicit non-goal here (open question #1).
5. **Kick/leave while in nether** — routed by `conn.dimension`; the offline slice self-stamps `dimension:"nether"` and the player rejoins there.
6. **Portal broken while someone's in the nether** — no stranding: return-travel re-validates the frame (`tickPortalDwell` backstop, `portal.ts:198-201`) and `ensureArrivalPortal` finds-or-builds on the overworld side.
7. **Both players dwell simultaneously** — the travel queue processes both in one tick; the second finds the shard already created; each gets its own `dim`+sync. Unit-tested.
8. **Backpressure during the worldSync burst** — travel syncs bypass shedding exactly like join syncs; a conn past the 1 MB kick threshold is already on the strike path. The traveler simply misses that tick's source-shard frame (they've left it).
9. **Prediction ledger across the swap** — new engine + `ledger.clear()` + `delayCtl.reset()` + buffer wipes in `adoptDimension`; stale poses/cmds are dropped server-side via `d`.
10. **Chat & roster** — global; roster entries carry `dim`; the panel shows "· Nether".
11. **Owner-kick of a nether player** — `kick`→`leave` routed by shard; unit-tested.
12. **Peaceful switch** — room mirrors `setWorldDifficulty` into every shard so hostiles despawn in **both** engines; unit-tested.
13. **Travel toast for others** — `playerDim` → synthetic `playerDimension` event → `flashMessage` in the drain (`useMinecraftGame.ts` switch).
14. **Reconnect mid/post-travel** — resumed `welcome.dimension` compared against the replica; mismatch triggers `adoptDimension` before the resync.
15. **Cross-dimension mobsKeyframe** — structurally impossible after shard scoping (would otherwise mass-prune the wrong replica's mobs).
16. **Sleep** — only overworld players gate the skip (free from the split); `wakeToMorning`'s clock jump mirrors to the nether shard each tick.

## 5. Memory / topology plan

- **Light bake resolved:** renderer-only (see §1). Headless skip saves ~39.3 MB + the full-world BFS per server engine.
- **Budget:** engine ≈ 39.3 MB blocks (+ objects); two-shard room ≈ 80 MB ≈ today's documented single-engine budget (~74 MB). **Keep `server/fly.toml` at MAX_ROOMS=3 / 512 MB** (worst case ~240 MB + Bun runtime); update the fly.toml comment and `docs/online.md` capacity note ("~80 MB per nether-active room after the light-skip; 6 rooms ≈ 1 GB" replaces the current text at `docs/online.md:249-253`).
- **Lifecycle:** lazy create on first travel/nether-join; linger-evict (60 s default) after the last nether player leaves — persist the section, drop the engine. One-time synchronous ctor hitch on the shared tick thread (all rooms pause briefly); measure with loadSim and document; the same class of hitch already exists at room load (`roomRegistry.ts:38-45`).

## 6. Test plan

- **Unit — engine:** headless light-skip; ctor dimension override; `ensureArrival`; `setWorldDifficulty`; mounted-dwell gate; dimension-guarded bed respawn.
- **Unit — protocol:** v4 field round-trips; `d` validation on pose/cmd; new message shapes.
- **Unit — room (`server/room.test.ts`, fakeSink pattern):** shard refactor parity; travel handoff (player moves engines, latch set, `dim`+sync sent, `playerDim` broadcast, SelfDelta shadow reset); dimension-scoped tick/keyframe fan-out; stale-`d` frame dropping; lag-comp partition; simultaneous dwell; join-in-nether; kick/leave-in-nether; Peaceful in both engines; persistence composition round-trip (nether builds + nether players + offline merge); shard linger-evict + rebuild.
- **Unit — session (`NetworkSession.test.ts`, FakeSocket):** the swap (engine replaced, socket alive, ledger/buffers cleared, self position adopted, `d` stamping flips); `playerDim` prune/adopt; nether welcome; stale-sync ignore; reconnect-into-other-dimension.
- **e2e:** new two-context nether journey (Phase 6); existing `multiplayer.e2e.ts` and SP `portal.e2e.ts` stay green.
- **Soak:** `loadSim` before/after with a nether-active room; report `slowestTickMs` p95 + `kbOutPerSec` in the PR.

## 7. Docs (per AGENTS.md)

Covered per-phase and in Commit 10: `protocol.md` (v4 + bump/rollout), `deploy.md` (protocol-bump runbook — new), `online.md` (nether co-op + capacity), `architecture.md` (shards + client swap + dispose ownership), `manual.md` (portals now online), `tuning.md` (linger config, mounted gate), `testing.md` (coverage map), `save-format.md` (v18 **unchanged**; optional `spawnPoint.dimension` addition; server now writes `dimensions.nether`), `CHANGELOG.md`.

## 8. Open questions for the user

1. **In-nether respawn design:** keep the current in-dimension respawn (this plan), or Minecraft-style "no bed → overworld world-spawn" (requires respawn-time shard handoff — meaningful extra room surgery)? Plan assumes keep.
2. **Pets don't travel** (SP parity) — acceptable for this branch?
3. **e2e scope:** full frame-build-by-cmd journey (flagged flake risk) vs. trimming to ignition-onward if CI proves the build helper unstable?
4. **Fly sizing:** confirm keeping MAX_ROOMS=3 @ 512 MB (the light-skip pays for the second engine) — no VM bump planned.
5. **Nether shard linger** default 60 s and its config home (server env like `COMMAND_LOG_SIZE` vs. `lib/game/config.ts`) — plan proposes a server env var.

**High-risk files (largest/subtlest diffs):** `server/room.ts` (tick/fan-out core rewrite), `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts` (closure rebinding for the engine swap), `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts` (ctor dimension resolution + portal gate), `components/GameShell.tsx` + `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts` (session-dispose ownership move).

# Nether in Multiplayer (`feat/nether-online`, protocol v3→v4)

## Context

v0.16.0 shipped the Nether as a single-player-only feature: `GameEngine.portalsEnabled` (`lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts:535-537`, `authority === "local" && !replica`) makes the server engine and every online replica refuse portal ignition and dwell, so the co-op audience — the other flagship investment (v0.13 multiplayer, MP v2, protocol v3 lag comp) — cannot see the Nether at all. The user picked "Nether online" as the next epic: online worlds can ignite/use portals, players can split across dimensions, and everything replicates.

Exploration verdict: the **save layer is already done** (v18 `DimensionSection`, per-player `dimension`/`portalArrival`; the server room round-trips nether bytes verbatim via `foreignDimensions`). Every obstacle is in the runtime and the wire: one engine = one dimension fixed at construction (`state.ts:306-313`), protocol v3 has zero dimension awareness, tick fan-out is global with no interest filter (`server/room.ts:442-473`), and the lag-comp mob-history ring is dimension-less (`server/mobHistory.ts`).

**User decisions (2026-07-10):** in-Nether death respawns in the Nether (SP parity, no cross-dimension respawn); pets stay behind on travel (SP parity, follow-up candidate). Fly stays at 512 MB — the headless light-skip (below) pays for the second engine.

## Architecture: two engines per room ("dimension shards")

Preserves the load-bearing invariant "one engine = one dimension" everywhere; every engine system already works per-dimension unmodified. Rejected: multi-world `GameState` (rewrites ~20 system files, breaks SP), reconnect-per-travel/second room (doubles MAX_ROOMS pressure, persist races on one `worlds` row, full-disconnect UX per portal).

70:**Game modes.** The four modes (`survival`/`creative`/`adventure`/`spectator`, `lib/game/gameModes.ts`) are a single `state.gameMode` axis. Systems gate on **intent predicates** rather than the raw id, so all four share one set of seams: `takesDamage` switches off the three damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts` (covering fall/void/lava/water/drown/mob/poison at once) plus hunger/regen/oxygen in `playerStats.ts`; `canEditBlocks`/`freeBuild` gate breaking and placing in `mining.ts`; `canInteract` gates the interaction commands in `dispatch`; `canFly`/`isNoclip` drive flight and the collision skip in `playerMotion.ts` (and the auto-unstuck skip in `step`); `mobsThreaten` folds into `activeHostile` in `mobAI.ts`; `usesInventory`/`takesDamage` hide HUD elements. `gameMode` rides the per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` → a v8 `SaveData` field → `GameEngine`), but unlike `worldType` it's **switchable in-game** — `setGameMode` (`GameEngine.switchGameMode`) resets transient hazard timers, bars, flight, and noclip-entombment on the change. The transient `isFlying` is never serialized.
76:**Advancements & statistics.** Progression meta (`systems/advancements.ts`) hangs off the **single `GameEngine.emit` chokepoint** every system already emits through: `emit(event, actorId?)` pushes the event for the shell, then runs `observeProgress` — `recordEvent` folds it into the acting player's `stats` counters (a `Map<string, number>`), and `evaluateAdvancements` unlocks any advancement whose threshold the new stats just crossed, adding it to that player's `advancements` (a `Set`) and emitting `advancementUnlocked` (the one event type `emit` skips, to avoid recursing). **Per-player attribution** (co-op): the actor is an explicit `actorId` (a kill's killer via `removeMobAt`, a death's victim) if given, else whoever's per-player `stepPlayer`/`dispatch` is currently running (`actingPlayer`), else the primary — so each player scores their own mining/kills/crafts and a playerless server room with no attributable actor scores nothing. Kill credit resolves through `MobState.lastHitByPlayer`, stamped by every player-attributed hit (melee/arrow/spear/pet-bite) so even a delayed sweep death (daylight burn, explosion) credits the right player; a replica never scores (the server owns it and streams each player's advancements/stats back on the `SelfDelta`). Tick-driven display stats (distance, play time) bump directly in `step` via `recordTick`, off the unlock path. Both `stats` and `advancements` persist in save v13 and, like `xp` and unlike `effects`, are **kept across death** (`clearEffects` never touches them). The L-key overlay (`AdvancementsPanel`) reads detail through `GameApi.advancementState()` pulled on render — only the open flag and the unlocked **count** ride the snapshot, so play never churns it with stat values the HUD doesn't show.
86:- `GameRenderer.ts` — scene/camera/WebGL/lighting; `sync(state)` maps simulation state to visuals each frame; `dispose()` frees every GPU resource. WebGL creation returns `{ ok: false, error }` instead of throwing.
89:- **Per-voxel lighting**: the world/glass materials are patched via `onBeforeCompile` (`patchVoxelLighting`) to consume the baked `aLight` attribute — they gate the scene-lit colour by sky exposure (caves go dark) and add block light back as an albedo-tinted glow (torches/lava light the dark). **Day/night needs no uniform and no re-mesh**: the scene sun + hemisphere already scale with `daylight` in `syncDayNight`, so a sky-exposed surface dims at night through the scene lights while caves stay dark regardless. 98:- **Atmosphere** (all procedural, zero assets, freed in `dispose()`): `particleSystem.ts` + the pure, unit-tested `particlePool.ts` draw event-driven bursts (block shards from `BLOCK_COLORS`, mob-death puffs, eat crumbs, jump/land/footstep dust) as one `THREE.Points` with a soft-sprite shader, spawned via `GameRenderer.handleEvent(event, state)` (wired into the event drain beside `audio.handleEvent`). `skyView.ts` + the pure `starField.ts` layer camera-following stars, a moon, a sun disc, and drifting canvas-noise clouds over the day-night sky lerp, ramped by `daylight`. `precipitation.ts` is the camera-following rain/snow field driven by `state.weather`, and `syncDayNight` adds the matching overcast sky tint + dimmed light + nearer fog.

None affect single-player, and none are save-sensitive.

- **`ROOM_CAPACITY`** (`8`, protocol.ts) — max players per world. The v1 co-op
  scale the whole design assumes; raising it grows the per-tick pose/self fan-out
  quadratically, so re-measure with `loadSim` before nudging it.
- **`MAX_ROOMS`** (env, default `6`) — worlds one process hosts (memory: ~74 MB
  each). Joins beyond it are refused at the door, not thrashed. Tune from
  `/rooms` p95 tick + peak memory.
- **Tick rate** — `TICK_SECONDS` (`0.05` = 20 Hz, `tickDriver.ts`) is the room
  sim + pose-stream cadence. The whole latency budget hangs off it; not a
  casual dial.
- **Replication cadence** — `KEYFRAME_INTERVAL_TICKS` (`100` = 5 s, full mob
  keyframe / drift correction), mob delta frames at **10 Hz** (half tick rate)
---

  dockerfile = 'Dockerfile'

[env]
  # Sized to the 512 MB VM below: ~74 MB/room + the Bun runtime. Raise memory
  # and MAX_ROOMS together (docs/deploy.md) — 6 rooms needs ~1 GB.
  MAX_ROOMS = '3'
  PERSISTENCE = 'postgres'

[http_service]
  internal_port = 8080

 */

content.content:
docs/architecture.md:89:- **Per-voxel lighting**: the world/glass materials are patched via `onBeforeCompile` (`patchVoxelLighting`) to consume the baked `aLight` attribute — they gate the scene-lit colour by sky exposure (caves go dark) and add block light back as an albedo-tinted glow (torches/lava light the dark). **Day/night needs no uniform and no re-mesh**: the scene sun + hemisphere already scale with `daylight` in `syncDayNight`, so a sky-exposed surface dims at night through the scene lights while caves stay dark regardless. The patch anchors on stable `ShaderChunk` includes; the e2e "renders without errors" smoke test guards it against a Three.js bump.
docs/architecture.md:151:- `lighting.ts` — per-voxel light (sky + block, packed 0–15 each into `world.light`). `computeFullLight` bakes the whole field from the blocks at load (top-down sunlight column pass + BFS bleed; block-light BFS from emitters); `applyEdit` patches it locally on each block edit with a Minecraft-style remove/refill flood. **Derived cache, never serialized** — a pure function of `world.blocks`. `opacity`/`emission` classify each block (air/glass transmit, water/leaves attenuate, torches/lava emit).
docs/architecture.md:154:- `meshing.ts` — `buildGeometryRegion(world, …)` with face culling, baked ambient occlusion, atlas UVs, and a per-vertex `aLight` (sky-exposure, block-light) sampled from the faced voxel; `buildGeometryLayersRegion` splits opaque terrain from clear glass for the renderer.
docs/architecture.md:167:4. **Arrival** — the fresh engine boots into the player's saved dimension: the dimension picks the generator (`generateWorld` vs `generateNetherWorld`) and the save section (`dimensionSectionOf`), and `ensureArrivalPortal` consumes `portalArrival` before the light bake — reusing the nearest portal within `PORTAL_SEARCH_RADIUS` or building one (stone pad, lit 2×3 frame) through `blockChanges`, so it persists as ordinary diff. The player lands inside the portal, latched.
docs/architecture.md:194:- **Lighting is a derived cache, never serialized**: `world.light` is a pure function of `world.blocks`, baked once at load (`computeFullLight`) and patched per edit (`applyEdit`), both in `lib/world/lighting.ts`. The bake/patch is wired in the **engine** (the constructor and `blockChanges.set`, the single chokepoint all gameplay edits flow through) — never the renderer — so the minimap-before-renderer `worldMeshDirty` ordering stays intact. Every new block needs a lighting class in `opacity`/`emission` (the default is opaque, no emission); sky light falls straight down a clear column for free at any level, so the bake's column pass and the incremental flood must agree (see `propagated`). `applyEdit`'s correctness is pinned by whole-array equivalence tests against a from-scratch bake.
docs/save-format.md:38:- per-player `portalArrival` (optional) — a one-shot arrival anchor written **only** by `serializeForTravel` (never by an ordinary save) and consumed at the next boot: the engine finds or builds the arrival portal there (`ensureArrivalPortal`) before the light bake, so the built portal persists as ordinary diff and the operation is idempotent across a crash

docs/architecture.md:89:- **Per-voxel lighting**: the world/glass materials are patched via `onBeforeCompile` (`patchVoxelLighting`) to consume the baked `aLight` attribute — they gate the scene-lit colour by sky exposure (caves go dark) and add block light back as an albedo-tinted glow (torches/lava light the dark). **Day/night needs no uniform and no re-mesh**: the scene sun + hemisphere already scale with `daylight` in `syncDayNight`, so a sky-exposed surface dims at night through the scene lights while caves stay dark regardless. The patch anchors on stable `ShaderChunk` includes; the e2e "renders without errors" smoke test guards it against a Three.js bump.
docs/architecture.md:151:- `lighting.ts` — per-voxel light (sky + block, packed 0–15 each into `world.light`). `computeFullLight` bakes the whole field from the blocks at load (top-down sunlight column pass + BFS bleed; block-light BFS from emitters); `applyEdit` patches it locally on each block edit with a Minecraft-style remove/refill flood. **Derived cache, never serialized** — a pure function of `world.blocks`. `opacity`/`emission` classify each block (air/glass transmit, water/leaves attenuate, torches/lava emit).
docs/architecture.md:154:- `meshing.ts` — `buildGeometryRegion(world, …)` with face culling, baked ambient occlusion, atlas UVs, and a per-vertex `aLight` (sky-exposure, block-light) sampled from the faced voxel; `buildGeometryLayersRegion` splits opaque terrain from clear glass for the renderer.
docs/architecture.md:167:4. **Arrival** — the fresh engine boots into the player's saved dimension: the dimension picks the generator (`generateWorld` vs `generateNetherWorld`) and the save section (`dimensionSectionOf`), and `ensureArrivalPortal` consumes `portalArrival` before the light bake — reusing the nearest portal within `PORTAL_SEARCH_RADIUS` or building one (stone pad, lit 2×3 frame) through `blockChanges`, so it persists as ordinary diff. The player lands inside the portal, latched.
docs/architecture.md:194:- **Lighting is a derived cache, never serialized**: `world.light` is a pure function of `world.blocks`, baked once at load (`computeFullLight`) and patched per edit (`applyEdit`), both in `lib/world/lighting.ts`. 190	Hard-won invariants — easy to silently break:
191	
192	- **Transparent blocks are explicit render layers**: `buildGeometryLayersRegion` sends glass to a blended, non-depth-writing material while opaque terrain keeps normal depth writes. Glass-to-glass and water-to-water internal faces are culled; opaque faces touching glass remain visible through it. Water still uses the opaque layer and all world materials are `THREE.DoubleSide` so water is visible from inside. New transparent blocks must extend both the layer routing and face-visibility rules. **Lava is the exception that proves the rule**: it is a normal _solid_ block, so the default opaque face-culling already shows only its surface — it needs no special routing. (It does need a lighting class — see below.)
193	
194	- **Lighting is a derived cache, never serialized**: `world.light` is a pure function of `world.blocks`, baked once at load (`computeFullLight`) and patched per edit (`applyEdit`), both in `lib/world/lighting.ts`. The bake/patch is wired in the **engine** (the constructor and `blockChanges.set`, the single chokepoint all gameplay edits flow through) — never the renderer — so the minimap-before-renderer `worldMeshDirty` ordering stays intact. Every new block needs a lighting class in `opacity`/`emission` (the default is opaque, no emission); sky light falls straight down a clear column for free at any level, so the bake's column pass and the incremental flood must agree (see `propagated`). `applyEdit`'s correctness is pinned by whole-array equivalence tests against a from-scratch bake.
195	
196	- **Lava and the head/body damage split**: lava is solid, so contact damage (`tickLavaExposure`) samples the block underfoot/at body height rather than immersion. Drowning (`tickOxygen`) keys on the _head_ (eye cell) and is deliberately separate from the body-keyed 60 s water-exposure timer — they coexist (one models holding your breath, the other prolonged immersion). All three transient timers/state reset on reload/respawn and are never serialized.
197	- **Doors are multi-cell state machines encoded as blocks**: four facings × open/closed × upper/lower produce 16 internal `BlockId`s. Placement and breaking update both cells atomically; interaction validates the matching pair before toggling. `doorBounds` drives both thin mesh geometry and AABB collision. `highestSolidY` ignores doors so mob surface-following cannot climb over them; mob movement still checks their panel collision and never calls the player-only interaction handler.

Hard-won invariants — easy to silently break:

- **Transparent blocks are explicit render layers**: `buildGeometryLayersRegion` sends glass to a blended, non-depth-writing material while opaque terrain keeps normal depth writes. Glass-to-glass and water-to-water internal faces are culled; opaque faces touching glass remain visible through it. Water still uses the opaque layer and all world materials are `THREE.DoubleSide` so water is visible from inside. New transparent blocks must extend both the layer routing and face-visibility rules. **Lava is the exception that proves the rule**: it is a normal _solid_ block, so the default opaque face-culling already shows only its surface — it needs no special routing. (It does need a lighting class — see below.)

- **Lighting is a derived cache, never serialized**: `world.light` is a pure function of `world.blocks`, baked once at load (`computeFullLight`) and patched per edit (`applyEdit`), both in `lib/world/lighting.ts`. The bake/patch is wired in the **engine** (the constructor and `blockChanges.set`, the single chokepoint all gameplay edits flow through) — never the renderer — so the minimap-before-renderer `worldMeshDirty` ordering stays intact. Every new block needs a lighting class in `opacity`/`emission` (the default is opaque, no emission); sky light falls straight down a clear column for free at any level, so the bake's column pass and the incremental flood must agree (see `propagated`). `applyEdit`'s correctness is pinned by whole-array equivalence tests against a from-scratch bake.

- **Lava and the head/body damage split**: lava is solid, so contact damage (`tickLavaExposure`) samples the block underfoot/at body height rather than immersion. Drowning (`tickOxygen`) keys on the _head_ (eye cell) and is deliberately separate from the body-keyed 60 s water-exposure timer — they coexist (one models holding your breath, the other prolonged immersion). All three transient timers/state reset on reload/respawn and are never serialized.
- **Doors are multi-cell state machines encoded as blocks**: four facings × open/closed × upper/lower produce 16 internal `BlockId`s. Placement and breaking update both cells atomically; interaction validates the matching pair before toggling. `doorBounds` drives both thin mesh geometry and AABB collision. `highestSolidY` ignores doors so mob surface-following cannot climb over them; mob movement still checks their panel collision and never calls the player-only interaction handler.

35:- `worldgenVersion` (optional) — the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` stamped by `serialize()`. `applyWorldgenGuard` (`lib/game/save.ts`), run first thing in the `GameEngine` constructor (one seam covering single-player, cloud saves, and the server room), enforces the staleness rule: a **mismatched** stamp discards every dimension's world half (changes, blockEntities, lootedChests, mobs, vehicles, dimensions, villagesSeeded) and the world reboots from its seed with the players kept. An **absent** stamp (anything migrated from ≤ v17) is grandfathered untouched — the guard only ever acts on a stamp it wrote itself
36:- `dimensions` (optional) — non-overworld world halves, currently `{ nether?: DimensionSection }`. A `DimensionSection` carries exactly the world-half fields (`changes`, `blockEntities?`, `lootedChests?`, `mobs?`, `vehicles?`) with voxel indices in **that dimension's** coordinate space. `dimensionSectionOf(save, dimension)` maps the overworld to the top level and other dimensions to their section, so restore code is dimension-agnostic. An engine re-emits sections it does not simulate **verbatim** (`foreignDimensions` / `foreignOverworld` on `GameEngine`) — the server room (always overworld) round-trips a world's nether builds without knowing they exist. ⚠️ **Drift trap:** a field added to `serialize()`'s world half must be added to `DimensionSection` too, or it silently stays overworld-global (pinned by the byte-equality pass-through test in `GameEngine.test.ts`)
37:- per-player `dimension` (optional) — where that player is (`"overworld"` | `"nether"`); absent ⇒ overworld. Restored by `restorePlayerDimension`; the engine boots into the **local player's** dimension (swap-on-travel: one live dimension per engine)
38:- per-player `portalArrival` (optional) — a one-shot arrival anchor written **only** by `serializeForTravel` (never by an ordinary save) and consumed at the next boot: the engine finds or builds the arrival portal there (`ensureArrivalPortal`) before the light bake, so the built portal persists as ordinary diff and the operation is idempotent across a crash
54:- **v18** (dimensions — the nether) — adds optional top-level `worldgenVersion` and `dimensions`, and optional per-player `dimension`/`portalArrival` (all described above). `migrateSaveV17toV18` is a **pure version bump**: no data moves — the top-level world fields remain the overworld's, so every pre-v18 save loads as an overworld-only world with the guard grandfathered (no stamp ⇒ never fires). The nether's own generator (`lib/world/netherGeneration.ts`) is a separate byte contract with its own SHA-256 baselines; adding it changed **no overworld bytes**, so `WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays **11** — but from here on a bump discards **both** dimensions' diffs together (one stamp governs the whole save). The `NetherPortal` `BlockId` (91) is appended and has no item; `Obsidian` (90) and the new items (buckets, flint & steel) are additive string ids.
92:`worldgenVersion` records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (`lib/game/config.ts`, currently 11) the world was generated under. This **replaces the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump**: when the worldgen baseline changes, bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, and a world whose recorded version differs has its stale block-diffs discarded and reboots from its stored seed — per-world, with no key rename and without touching unaffected worlds. Since save v18 the stamp also lives **inside the `SaveData` blob** and the discard is actually **enforced** at engine boot (`applyWorldgenGuard` — it was documentation-only before); the `WorldMeta` copy remains for the world list.

37	- per-player `dimension` (optional) — where that player is (`"overworld"` | `"nether"`); absent ⇒ overworld. Restored by `restorePlayerDimension`; the engine boots into the **local player's** dimension (swap-on-travel: one live dimension per engine)

39	
40	Each world's `SaveData` is stored in **IndexedDB** — database `monecraft`, object store `worldSaves`, keyed by world id (including the synthetic `cloud:<id>` ids) — as a structured clone of the object, not a JSON string, so it lives off localStorage's ~5–10 MB origin quota. The async store is `lib/game/saveStore.ts` (`worldSaves.read/write/remove/flushWrite`) over the minimal wrapper in `lib/game/idbKv.ts`; writes are queued per world with latest-wins coalescing, reads are read-your-writes (a remount can never see a stale blob), and `write()` resolves only when the transaction has durably committed. Validation and the migration chain live in `lib/game/save.ts` — every read (either container) flows through `parseSave`; the sync `readSave`/`writeSave` (injectable `Storage`) remain for the legacy localStorage keys `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` (`worldSaveKey` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`), which are now only a migration source, the store's fallback when IndexedDB is unavailable (some private modes — old behavior, quota risk included), and the server's save path (`server/persistence.ts`). `GameEngine.serialize()` produces the save from live state, and `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts` maintains the block diff. 41
